stimulus.text: In 1828 Noah Webster published An American Dictionary of the English Language. Webster gave American words American spellings: color for colour, center for centre, defense for defence, traveling for travelling. He wanted a dictionary that belonged to the United States, not to Britain.
stimulus.source_note: Paraphrase of Barron's Premium 2027, Chapter 6, Topic 4.9 A: Webster sought to codify a specifically American dictionary, separate from British English, publishing his American Dictionary of the English Language in 1828. Spelling examples are Webster's standard American forms. Original synthesis, not a quotation.

source: original; stimulus as described in the stimulus source note
stem: Which of the following would Webster's work most likely have encouraged?

options.text: American writers using American settings and American speech
Merchants importing more British books for American readers
options.misconception: American readers still bought British books, so it is easy to think Webster wanted more of them.

options.text: Churches returning to British prayer books
options.misconception: Churches and dictionaries are both books, so it is easy to connect them.

options.text: States adopting British common law without any change
options.misconception: American law did borrow from Britain, so it is easy to extend that borrowing to everything.

rationales.A: Once the language itself was declared American, writers could claim American subjects in American words.
rationales.B: Webster wanted Americans to rely less on Britain, not to import more British books.
rationales.C: Webster wrote about spelling and language, not about how churches should worship.
rationales.D: Webster's whole point was to change what America took from Britain, not to adopt it unchanged.
rationales.general:
1. Follow the logic of the dictionary. If American English is its own language, it deserves its own books.
2. Picture the next step. Writers take the hint and set stories in America, in American speech.
Background from the books: Irving and Cooper soon did exactly that, turning American places into literature.
Remember: when a people name their language as their own, their stories usually follow.
